text.p: The shorter end lost ground after the Institute of Public Credit Management rejected bids at its three-year bond sale, with the weakness of the Spanish market also contributing to the decline, traders said.
The fact that yields rose at the five-year auction also encouraged the negative mood, they said.
But several traders saw the market reasonably well supported at current levels, with the possibility of a rise in the year-on-year inflation rate for January already discounted.
The January numbers will be issued by the National Statistics Institute on Monday.
The longer end was following the German trend, traders said.
